## Why does traditional plant medicine exist?
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 55%;">

* **Humans have always searched for substances that relieve suffering and provide cures for loved ones**

<br/>

* **Mystical agents underlying the natural world were thought to cause illness, thus cures were sought from animals and plants**  
    + likely involved a painful process of trial and error

<br/>

* **Communication among early populations was poor...**
    + slowed accumulation/spread of medical knowledge
    + remedies discovered independently several times

 </div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:650px; WIDTH:400px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/witch.jpg">

## Histories of plants in medicine eventually recorded
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 55%;">

* **Earilest known medical document by Sumerians**
    + 4,000 years ago in Mesopotamia

<br/>

* **Herbal medicines were prevalent in ancient Egypt**
    + mandrake for pain, garlic for heart
    + remedies 'published' in Ebers Papyrus

<br/>

* **Ancient Chinese reveal herbal remedies**
    + Pun-tsao (1600) thousands of herbal remedies

<br/>

* **Aztecs gifted Badianus manuscript to king of Spain**
    + mesoamerican herbal remedies for 100 afflictions

 </div>


<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:190px; LEFT:650px; WIDTH:400px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/ebers.jpg">

## Ancient Greeks are the foundation of western medicine
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 64%;">

* **Greek physician, Hippocrates, Father of Medicine**
    + believed diseases had *natural* causes
    + used various herbal remedies
    + works used for 1500 years!

<br/>

* **Dioscorides, Roman military physician, wrote 'De Materia Medica' describing preparation of 1000 simple drugs**
    + 600 species of plants with medicinal value
    + very inaccurate but became a prototype

<br/>

* **Herbal remedies by Greeks/Romans have been kept and lost**
    + willow bark tea = precursor to asprin
    + *Ferula* used for contraception but collected to extinction

 </div>
 
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:190px; LEFT:725px; WIDTH:325px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/roman.jpg">

## Age of herbals: Doctrine of Signatures
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: right; width: 55%;">

* **Renaissance age (1500) & printing press created a revival of herbalism**
    + 4 German 'Fathers of Botany'
    + Gerard, "The herbal of general history of plants"

<br/>

* **Publishings included medicinal uses & superstitions**
    + Culpepper, "The complete herbal" included astrology
 
 <br/>
 
* **Doctrine of Signatures: herbs resembling various parts of the body can be used to treat ailments of those body parts**
    + juice of bloodwort treats blood disorders
    + lobed liverwort treats liver complaints

 </div>
 
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:240px; LEFT:5px; WIDTH:475px; HEIGHT:325px" SRC="images/culpper.jpg">

## 17-18th century added experimental approaches
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: right; width: 55%;">

* **Science and philosophy advanced to hypotheses testing stage**
    + helped discredit many previous approaches

<br/>

* **Improved understanding of human physiology led to more careful testing of medicines**

<br/>

* **Led to the discovery of vaccinations and documented experiments on plant medicines for heart problems (e.g., foxglove for dropsy)**
    + start of 'pharamacology'

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:50px; WIDTH:375px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/foxglove3.jpg">

## Modern era prescription drugs
<hr>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:645px; WIDTH:400px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/opium.jpg">

<div style="float: left; width: 58%;">

* **Herbalism diminished in recent centuries, but remedies still were effective**
    + remedies became 'prescriptions' by physicians
    + William Withering, 1775, foxglove for heart failure
    + new standard for pharmaceutical industry

<br/>

* **Purifying active extracts/synthetics started in 19^th^ century**
    + morphine from poppy in 1806
    + Salicyclic acid (many plants) synthesized for pain relief

<br/>

</div>

<div style="float: left; width: 99%;">

* **25% of prescriptions today contain plant-derived active ingredients**
    + research still investigating new active compounds
    + e.g. studying ingredients in Native America remedies

</div> 
 
## Modern era plant-based medicine
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 55%;">

* **First half of 20th century was a period of tremendous advancement as the causes of diseases were uncovered**

<br/>

* **Initially, many modern medicines were isolated, purified products from traditional plant-derived extracts**
    + morphine, quinine, ephedrine

<br/>

* **Chemists begin to determine the structures of these active compounds**
    + eventually leads to synthetic synthesis

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:630px; WIDTH:380px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/morphine.jpg">

## Reduction in natural remedies post 1950's
<hr>
<br/>   

<div style="float: left; width: 45%;">

* **Health care workers developed disdain for 'folk' based medicine**
    + belief that humans have 'tested-out' plants for medicinal value

<br/>   

* **Pharmaceutical companies are now reluctant to undertake massive screening and testing programs to explore for new plant drugs**
    + low ROI

<br/>

* **Advances in understanding the biochemistry of disease favor design of novel synthetic drugs**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:180px; LEFT:525px; WIDTH:575px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/trail.jpg">

## Is the philosophy of Western medicine a barrier?
<hr>
<br/>

* **Western medicine philosophy: emphasis on diagnosis of explicit disease and treatment with with one/few specific compounds**

<br/>

* **Different practices of medicine treat illnesses more holistically**
    + ailments are manifestations of an imbalance
    
<br/>

* **In these alternate practices, plant-based medicine is far more common**
    + in recent decades these approaches have increased in the US/Europe

<br/>    
    
* **Across approaches to medicine, the role of plant biodiversity remain vital**
    + emerging diseases/strains vs compounds discovered from plants

## National Cancer Institute: Natural Products Discovery Program
<hr>
<br/> 

**Since 1986, the Developmental Therapeutics Program at NCI has empowered the program to acquire plants and marine organisms through collection contracts**

<br/> 

<div style="float: left; width: 55%;">

**Encompasses >25 tropical and subtropical countries worldwide**

<br/> 

* **80k plant samples (green)**
    + 5K unique genera
<br/> 

* **25K marine invertebrates and algae (blue)**
    + 4K unique genera
<br/> 

* **25K microbial samples (brownish)**
    + 1K unique genera
<br/> 

* **over 230,000 unique extracts**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:300px; LEFT:590px; WIDTH:520px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/samples.png">
 
## Herbal medicine today
<hr>

<div style="float: left; width: 64%;">

* **Rural populations still rely on herbal medicine**
    + China, India, S. America, Africa, & Appalachia
    + medicine + supplements industry value = ~250 million

<br/>

* **Modern Chinese medicine combines herbal, acupuncture & Western medicine**
    + unique health care from 1 billion people
    + thousands of medicinal herbs

<br/>

* **Modern Indian culture believe in traditional medicine**
    + manufactured pharmaceuticals too expensive
    + reliance on indigenous cures

<br/>

* **Rainforests are hubs of medical potential, but are decreasing**
    + loss of tribal herbal practices

 </div>
 
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:190px; LEFT:675px; WIDTH:375px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/plotkin.jpg">

## Active principals in plants
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: right; width: 60%;">

* **Medicine value tied to chemical compounds**
    + manufactured by biochemical pathways

<br/>

* **Compounds called 'secondary products' as they do not directly impact metabolism (growth)**
    + alkaloids, glycosides, terpenes & phenolics

<br/>

* **Herbivore defense, inhibit fungal or bacteria pathogens**

 </div>
 
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:220px; LEFT:25px; WIDTH:400px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/secondary.png">

## Alkaloids and Glycosides
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: right; width: 55%;">

* **Alkaloids: diverse compounds found in dicots**
    + analegstics - pain reduction
    + impact animal nervous/muscle systems
    + medicinal, poisonous, hallucinogenic
    + *caffeine, nicotine, cocaine, morphine, quinine*

<br/>

* **Glycosides: widespread compounds with glucose**
    + cyanogenic or cardioactive glycosides, saponins
    + steroid molecules as active component
    + treat heart failure, can be toxic
    + digitalis, lily of the valley, oleander
    
 </div>
 
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:210px; LEFT:25px; WIDTH:400px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/alkaloids2.jpg">

## Medicinal plant case study: Foxglove
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 70%;">

* **Foxglove (*digitalis purpurea*) bienneial in snapdragon family**
    + lawn ornamental
    + 30 different glycosides
    + can be very toxic

<br/>

* **Digitoxin no longer a front-line drug today but still used on hundreds of thousands of patients**
    + thin line between theraputic and toxic

<br/>

* **In 1775, British physician learned of a folk remedy for dropsy**
    + bloating due to fluid accumulation: congestive heart failure
    + digitalis tea became treatment
    + slows heart rate, increase strength of heartbeat
    
</div>
  
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:190px; LEFT:800px; WIDTH:225px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/foxglove2.jpg">

## Medicinal plant case study: Willow to aspirin
<hr
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 60%;">

* **Willow tree bark used for pain reduction in many cultures**
    + ancient Greeks and Native Americans
    + reduces fever and chills

<br/>

* **Evolution of aspirin began with willow bark experiments in England**
    + 1828, salicin isolated as active ingredient
    + salicin derivatives occur in many species

<br/>

* **BAYER focused on acetylsalicylic acid from *Spirea*  plant**
    + less digestive issues
    + renamed to *aspirin*

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:185px; LEFT:640px; WIDTH:525px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/aspirin.jpg">

## Medicinal plant case study: Fever Bark Tree
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 59%;">

* **Malaria is one of the worlds most prevalent diseases**
    + 200 million infections each year
    + records of malaria date back to ancient Egyptians
    + female *Anopheles* mosquite w/ *Plasmodium* parasite
  
 <br/>   

* **Fever bark tree was first treatment for malaria**
    + native to east slopes of Andes mtns
    + belongs to coffee family
    + used by Incas to treat fever, then malaria
 
<br/>
  
* **Trade developed for powdered bark**
    + 2lbs to treat one person
    + *quinine* was isolated before over-exploitation
    + now: synthetic cholroquinine

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:190px; LEFT:620px; WIDTH:400px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/plantation.jpg">

## Medicinal plant case study: Ephedra
<hr>

* **Ephedrine is a plant alkaloid produced by genu *Ephedra* **
    + only one genus in the family of gymnosperms
    + native to Americas, Europe, Asia & Africa

<br/>

* **Long cultural history as a herbal medicine**
    + decongestant and respiratory ailments

<br/>

* **Ephedrine still found in modern drugs**
    + relaxes bronchial muscles & a CNS stimulant

<br/>

* **Large scale abuse of herbal *Ephedra* products**
    + herbal ecstasy, similar to amphetamines
    + activates thermogenesis, calorie burning
    + supplements illegal, medications?

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:230px; LEFT:600px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:350px" SRC="images/epedra.jpg">

## Medicinal plants and cancer
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 65%;">

* **Humans have suffered cancer for 1,000s of years**
    + Ebers Papyrus suggested treatments
    + 2^nd^  leading cause of death in US
    
<br/>

* **Plants have always featured in folk remedies**
    +  search for anticancer plant sources began in 50's by NCI
    + 1,000s of plants have been screened
    + several now part of chemotherapy treatments

<br/>

* **Vinca alkaloids for leukemia (Madagascar periwinkle)**
* **Taxol from Pacific yew used in many chemotherapy treatments**
* **Camptotheca from Chinese happy tree for ovarian cancer**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:220px; LEFT:745px; WIDTH:200px; HEIGHT:300px" SRC="images/taxol.jpg">

## Herbal remedies: promises and problems
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: right; width: 60%;">

* **Plants and plant extracts feature prominently in alternative medicines**
    + considered dietary supplements by FDA
    + multi-billion  a year industry

<br/>

* **Dietary supplements are not subject to FDA approval**
    + no rigorous clinical testing
    + FDA will only take reactionary actions

<br/>

* **Secondary plant compounds may have health benefits or cause adverse reactions**
    + 40% of US populations uses alternative medicines
    + no clinical linkage to medications

</div>
